query: Explain why some Qatar Airways Business-Class flights receive a non-recommended (Recommended = no) result.

per_column.name: seat_product_downgrade
per_column.rationale: A candidate cause: receiving a downgraded seat product (qsuite->standard, standard->older) plausibly drives dissatisfaction and non-recommendation. This is a treatment whose effect on the outcome is being attributed, surfaced from the reviews rather than named in the query.

per_column.name: seat_change_notification_given
per_column.rationale: Whether the passenger was notified of a seat change plausibly relates to whether a downgrade occurred (or was salient) and independently affects perceived fairness/outcome. However it is closely tied to the downgrade treatment; its status as a pure common cause is weak, and it borders on a mediator of the downgrade experience.

per_column.name: seat_product_generation
per_column.rationale: The generation of the seat (new flat bed vs older angled) is a common cause: it drives whether a 'downgrade' is experienced AND directly affects comfort and the recommendation outcome. Surfaced from data, not in query.

per_column.name: cabin_crew_service_quality
per_column.rationale: Crew service quality plausibly affects the outcome directly and correlates with overall operational quality; but relative to the seat-downgrade treatment it is more of an alternative independent cause than a strict common cause of the treatment. Treated conservatively as a competing-cause/confounder-like variable, not named in query.

per_column.name: service_consistency_across_legs
per_column.rationale: A separate quality signal (consistency across legs) affecting the outcome, but not plausibly a common cause of the seat-downgrade treatment. It is an alternative predictor of the outcome, not a genuine confounder.

per_column.name: food_beverage_quality
per_column.rationale: An alternative independent driver of the outcome. It does not plausibly cause the seat-downgrade treatment, so it is not a confounder of the downgrade->outcome relationship.

per_column.name: ffp_elite_status_failure
per_column.rationale: Elite status recognition failure can plausibly correlate with how a passenger is treated (e.g. downgrade risk / handling) and independently affects the recommendation outcome. Surfaced from data, not named in query; plausibility modest.

judge.rationale: The set does supply a clear TREATMENT (seat_product_downgrade) around the non-recommendation outcome, and none of the variables were named in the query, so anything relevant was genuinely surfaced from the text/data. However most added columns (food_beverage_quality, service_consistency_across_legs, cabin_crew_service_quality) function as ALTERNATIVE INDEPENDENT CAUSES/predictors of the outcome rather than genuine common causes of BOTH the downgrade treatment and the outcome. Only seat_product_generation is a fairly convincing common cause (it governs what counts as a downgrade and drives comfort/outcome); notification and elite-status-failure are weak, partly mediator-like confounders. The design leans toward regressing many outcome-drivers rather than deliberately adjusting for confounders of a defined treatment, so confounder quality is modest.
